p|panel|borrado_articulo_acceso_au: Australian Privacy Principle 12 (access) of the Privacy Act 1988
p|panel|borrado_articulo_acceso_nz: Information Privacy Principle 6 (access) of the Privacy Act 2020
p|panel|borrado_articulo_acceso_br: Article 18, item II, of the LGPD (access to the data)
p|panel|borrado_articulo_acceso_mx: Mexico’s federal law on the protection of personal data held by private parties
p|panel|borrado_articulo_acceso_co: Article 8(a) of Law 1581 of 2012 (to know my data) and its Article 14 (queries)
p|panel|borrado_articulo_acceso_cl: Article 12 of Law 19.628 (information about my data)
p|panel|borrado_plazo_acceso_co: 10 working days from the date of receipt, extendable by up to 5 more working days if you tell me why (Article 14)
p|panel|borrado_plazo_acceso_ar: ten calendar days from receiving this request (Article 14, paragraph 2)
p|panel|borrado_plazo_acceso_pe: the period the Regulation of Law 29733 sets for access requests
p|panel|borrado_asunto_acceso: Request for access to my personal data — {empresa}
p|panel|borrado_carta_acceso:
To the data protection officer of {empresa}:

My name is {nombre} and I am writing to exercise my right of access under {articulo} ({ley}).

Please tell me:
1. Whether you process personal data about me and, if so, which, in a copy I can read.
2. Where you obtained it, what you use it for and on what legal basis.
3. Whom you have shared or sold it to, in particular advertising companies or data brokers.
4. How long you keep it, and whether you make automated decisions or profiles about me with it.

Please answer within the period the law sets: {plazo}.

You can reply to this email: {correo}. If you need any further detail to find me in your systems, tell me; I am not sending more than necessary.
{evidencia}
{fecha}

{nombre}
p|panel|exp_queja_vence: Counted from the day it was sent, the deadline was {vence}.
p|panel|exp_queja_sin_dias: {dias} days have passed since I sent it.
p|panel|exp_queja_no_respondio: To this day I have received no answer.
p|panel|ct_lead: GUARDIANA learns which companies each program on this computer normally talks to. If a program starts contacting new companies (after an update, for example), it tells you calmly, with the before and the after, and you decide.
p|panel|ct_como: For its first {dias} days (or {n} launches spread over more than a day) GUARDIANA only learns and flags nothing. After that, it watches.
p|panel|ct_limite: What GUARDIANA sees is that a program asked where a company's server is. Asking is not sending data: we do not know what it sent, or whether it sent anything.
p|panel|ct_limite_corte: The block is the usual one, by name and for this computer. Windows says which program asked a second later, so the first query to a new company has already been answered: the block starts from the next one. And it applies to any program on this computer that asks for that name.
p|panel|ct_solo_windows: Knowing which program asked for each name is only possible on Windows: on this system there are no contracts to learn.
p|panel|ct_vacio: No programs yet. As soon as Windows says which program asks for each name, they will appear here.
p|panel|ct_avisos_ninguno: No program has started contacting new companies. Everything is as it was learnt.
p|panel|ct_aviso_version: {programa} {version} has changed: it started contacting {n} new companies
p|panel|ct_aviso_version_uno: {programa} {version} has changed: it started contacting a new company
p|panel|ct_aviso_archivo: {programa} was updated (its file is a different one): it started contacting {n} new companies
p|panel|ct_aviso_archivo_uno: {programa} was updated (its file is a different one): it started contacting a new company
p|panel|ct_aviso_nota: GUARDIANA saw it ask for their names; that does not say what it sent, or whether it sent anything.
p|panel|ct_fijar_explica: With the contract fixed, whatever this program starts contacting outside what was learnt is blocked by itself, and recorded.
p|panel|ct_motivo_navegador: It is a browser: it talks to the websites you visit, so «new» means nothing.
p|panel|ct_motivo_compartido: It is a shared Windows process: it asks on behalf of many services and Windows does not say which.
p|panel|ct_motivo_variado: While learning it contacted too many companies to have a contract: it behaves like a browser.
p|panel|ct_version_desconocida: Windows gave no version for it
p|panel|ct_sin_firma: Windows did not say who signs it
p|panel|ct_sin_cortar_esperado: {empresa}: not blocked, the computer needs it (certificates, updates, time)
p|panel|ct_reglas_hechas: {n} block rules, visible and reversible in «Rules»
p|panel|ct_reglas_hechas_uno: 1 block rule, visible and reversible in «Rules»
p|panel|ct_historial_lead: Every change goes into a chained register, like the extract: if someone deletes or changes a row, the check says so.
p|panel|ct_comprobado_ok: The register is whole: {n} rows, each linked to the one before.
p|panel|ct_comprobado_mal: The register does not add up from row {id} on.
p|panel|ct_comprobado_cola: Rows are missing at the end of the register.
p|panel|ct_pill_atencion: Attention: {n} programs started contacting new companies
p|panel|ct_cortadas: Blocked (by you or by the fixed contract)
p|panel|ct_hecho_cortar: Blocked. What was new for {programa} gets no answer on this computer any more.
p|panel|ct_hecho_aceptar: Accepted: it is now part of what is normal for {programa}.
p|panel|ct_hecho_deshacer: Block undone: those companies are now part of {programa}'s contract.
p|panel|ct_interruptor_nuevo: What is new for {programa}: allowed or blocked
p|panel|exp_lead: Every request you make to a company, with its legal deadline and what happened: that it delete your data or tell you what it holds. GUARDIANA counts the days, warns you when the deadline is up and prepares the complaint to the authority if they do not answer. Everything stays on this computer.
p|panel|exp_nuevo_lead: Pick the company (the ones at the top are those the devices in your home asked for most), what you ask it and the place whose law protects you.
p|panel|exp_empresa_desconocida: We do not know that company. Type its name as the Snapshot shows it, or its web address (example.com).
p|panel|exp_vacio: No case files yet. Open one here, or from “Get your data deleted” or a company’s profile.
p|panel|exp_frase_preparada: The letter is prepared. When you send it, press “I sent it” so the clock starts.
p|panel|exp_frase_sin_plazo_acceso: We have not checked the period this law gives to answer an access request: we only note the day you sent it.
p|panel|exp_resultado_pidio_identidad: They asked me to identify myself or for more details
p|panel|exp_resultado_denegado: They refused, in whole or in part
p|panel|exp_quitar_seguro: Remove this case file? This cannot be undone.
p|panel|exp_carta_explica: The same letter, in case you need it again: as a PDF to attach, opened in your mail or copied. Your name and email never leave this computer.
p|panel|exp_queja_explica: The deadline has passed. This is the complaint, already written with the dates: download it as a PDF or open it in your mail, attach the letter you sent and file it where the authority says.
p|panel|exp_notas_ph: Whatever you want to remember about this case (no personal data: it is kept as is on this computer).
p|panel|exp_aviso_pronto: {n} are due in the next few days
p|panel|exp_aviso_pronto_uno: 1 is due in the next few days
p|panel|exp_desde_borrado: The clocks from “Get your data deleted” now live here.
p|panel|exp_abrir_desde_ficha: Open a case file with this letter
p|panel|exp_abierto_ok: Case file opened. When you send the letter, mark it in Case files so the clock starts.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_en_expedientes: Every letter you mark as sent goes to Case files, where its deadline is counted, the answer noted and the complaint prepared.
p|panel|borrado_plazo_acceso_br: 15 days from the date of my request, with a clear and complete statement (Article 19, item II)
p|panel|exp_queja_solicitud_borrado: a request to delete my personal data
p|panel|exp_queja_solicitud_acceso: a request for access to my personal data
p|panel|av_lead: Your antivirus is the program with the most access to your computer: it checks all your files and, often, the pages you visit. This screen shows which internet addresses it contacts and what its own maker says about each one. Someone independent and open source has to watch the watcher.
p|panel|av_limite: What GUARDIANA can see: the name of every address the antivirus processes ask for on this computer. What it cannot see: the content of what it sends; anything sent without asking Windows for those names (through its own resolver or to a fixed address), or anything downloaded through other Windows programs such as Windows Update.
p|panel|av_vistos_lead: Last seven days. Each table lists first the addresses the maker does not document.
p|panel|av_ninguno: In the last {dias} days no antivirus on our list asked for addresses on this computer. If you use one that is not listed, write to us and we will add it.
p|panel|av_ocultos: There are {n} devices that do not share their detail with the home panel, so their antivirus is not shown here.
p|panel|av_ocultos_uno: There is 1 device that does not share its detail with the home panel, so its antivirus is not shown here.
p|panel|av_sin_firma: Windows did not say who signs this program. An unsigned process carrying an antivirus name might not be that antivirus.
p|panel|av_no_documentados: {n} with no purpose published by the maker
p|panel|av_no_documentados_uno: 1 with no purpose published by the maker
p|panel|av_col_que_es: What it is for, according to the maker
p|panel|av_mas: And {n} more addresses, with fewer queries.
p|panel|av_nombre_de: A {empresa} server; the maker does not say what it uses it for.
p|panel|av_uso_muestras: Upload of suspicious files for analysis
p|panel|av_uso_configuracion: Settings and features the maker switches on remotely
p|panel|av_uso_certificados: Checking that security certificates are still valid
p|panel|av_uso_otros: General product operation, no further detail
p|panel|av_historial_titulo: Each antivirus: what its terms say and what authorities decided
p|panel|av_historial_lead: For each antivirus on the list, installed or not: what its privacy policy and its contract say, in plain words and with a link for each sentence, and the fines, orders, rulings, bans, warnings and undertakings by public authorities, each with its official source.
p|panel|av_historial_limite: We only include decisions by public authorities with a published official source. We leave out lawsuits between private parties, settlements without a decision and press reports. If a decision was appealed or partly annulled, we say so.
p|panel|av_sin_sanciones: We are not aware of any published official decision about this product.
p|panel|av_terminos_nota: GUARDIANA’s summary of the maker’s own documents, sentence by sentence. It is not legal advice: the official text prevails, and it changes when the maker changes it. If something is wrong, write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
p|panel|av_tema_marketing: What else it uses it for
p|panel|av_como_1: Windows reports which program asked for each address and who signs that program. GUARDIANA recognizes each antivirus’s processes by their file name, using a public list we maintain (antivirus.txt).
p|panel|av_como_2: Next to each address we show what it is for according to the maker’s own documentation, with the link. If the maker does not document it, we say so without accusing anyone: it may be a legitimate service they have not published. You have the right to ask them.
p|panel|av_como_3: If you want to know what data your antivirus company holds about you, “Get your data deleted” prepares the letter to ask for it or to ask them to delete it.
p|panel|av_nunca: GUARDIANA will never ask you to turn off your antivirus. Watching it does not mean removing it: it is still a protection you need.
p|panel|esc_lead: What the program's own antivirus saw. It knows {n} sites this computer asks for.
p|panel|esc_lead_aprende: In its first days it learns which sites this computer asks for; meanwhile the “first time” rule only warns about programs downloaded from the internet. The other rules are already watching.
p|panel|esc_vacio: No warnings: it has seen nothing of what it watches.
p|panel|esc_cuarentena_lead: Files set aside and encrypted: they cannot run. Only those the shield flagged go in, and never those in Windows' folder or the installed programs'. “Put back” leaves them exactly where they were, exactly as they were.
